_comment: Published heat-mortality exposure-response coefficients for Indian cities. Consumed by backend/app/services/health.py to produce a RELATIVE-RISK index. These are literature values from peer-reviewed studies, NOT locally fitted to Ahmedabad outcome data. Every API response derived from this file must carry evidence=MODELLED_UNCALIBRATED and calibration_status=not_validated_locally.
usage_note: effect values are PERCENT CHANGE in daily all-cause mortality on exposed days vs unexposed days. relative_risk = 1 + (effect_pct / 100).

de_bont_2024.citation: de Bont J, Nori-Sarma A, Stafoggia M, et al. Impact of heatwaves on all-cause mortality in India: A comprehensive multi-city study. Environ Int. 2024;184:108461.
de_bont_2024.study_design: Two-stage time-series; quasi-Poisson GAM per city, random-effects meta-analysis
adjustments: penalized spline of calendar day, 9 df/year
de_bont_2024.data_availability: CONFIDENTIAL - daily death counts not downloadable

rathi_2021.citation: Rathi SK, Sodani PR. Summer temperature and all-cause mortality from 2006 to 2015 for Hyderabad, India. Afr Health Sci. 2021;21(3):1474-1481.
rathi_2021.study_design: Descriptive + bivariate, Pearson correlation for lag
rathi_2021.exposure_variable: daily MAXIMUM temperature and Heat Index
rathi_2021.data_availability: Obtained from municipal Birth & Death Registration Dept - shows the request route

pooled_heatwave_effects._definition: heatwave = N consecutive days with daily mean temperature above the Pth annual percentile
pooled_heatwave_effects._effect_units: percent change in daily all-cause mortality vs non-heatwave days

entries.note: closest proxy to the IMD single-day heatwave declaration
observed in only 6 of 10 cities (Ahmedabad, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Varanasi)

city_specific._definition: 2 consecutive days above the 97th percentile of daily mean temperature

ahmedabad.note: STRONGEST effect of all 10 cities. This is the primary coefficient for HeatLens.

_range_across_cities.note: 7x spread across cities - city-specific coefficients matter, do not apply the pooled value to Ahmedabad

effect_modification._base: restricted to heatwaves of 2+ consecutive days above the 97th percentile

intensity.per_unit: 1 percent increase in mean heatwave temperature above the city's 97th percentile
intensity.note: STRONGEST modifier - use the mutually adjusted value

duration.note: attenuates to null once intensity is adjusted for - do NOT stack a duration term on top of intensity

timing_in_season.per_unit: 1 day later start within the summer season
timing_in_season.note: no evidence of harvesting/adaptation effect by season timing

absolute_threshold_effects._caution: descriptive study, weaker design than de_bont_2024; use only as a cross-check

lag_structure.note: effect peaks SAME DAY - supports plan_d's same-day scoring, but says nothing about the multi-day carryover Plan C models

implementation_notes.threshold_computation: The percentile thresholds are computable today from results/ahmedabad_daily_2010_2024.csv. plan_b.local_thresholds(daily, percentile=97.0) already implements exactly this. NOTE: the studies use daily MEAN temperature; the daily CSV carries ta_max and ta_min, so derive a mean or recompute from the hourly Open-Meteo file.
implementation_notes.consecutive_day_logic: services/ensemble.py already needs consecutive_hot_days for plan_d's CUMULATIVE_DEBT regime. Reuse that counter against the p97 threshold rather than writing a second one.
what_this_does_NOT_license: Do not output an absolute predicted death count.
Do not claim HeatLens is validated - these coefficients validate the TEMPERATURE-mortality link, not the HTSI/PHD indices.
Do not stack duration and intensity modifiers (duration attenuates to null when mutually adjusted).
Do not apply the pooled 14.7% to Ahmedabad - the city-specific value is 24.9%.
implementation_notes.honest_framing: 'Published studies of Ahmedabad 2008-2019 found ~25% higher daily mortality on 2-day heatwaves above the local 97th percentile. Today's conditions match that definition.' That is a defensible sentence. 'We predict 31 deaths tomorrow' is not.
